rounds.text: Cravatex Ltd is demonstrating a powerful and accelerating operational turnaround that the market has completely failed to price in, with trailing twelve-month sales growth surging to 48% [E17] alongside 3-year and 5-year compounded sales growth figures of 27% [E16] and 25% [E15] respectively, comfortably outpacing the sector median sales growth of 11.8% [E73]. This top-line momentum is converting into high-quality profitability, highlighted by a robust current ROE of 24.1% [E13] and a median ROE of 24% over both the last year [E29] and the last 3 years [E28], marking a dramatic structural improvement over its 10-year median ROE of 9% [E26]. The stock trades at a highly attractive P/E of 11.6x against a sector benchmark of 20.32x [E6], and an exceptional P/B of 0.66x relative to its sector benchmark of 1.54x [E7], while rewarding patient shareholders with a healthy dividend yield of 3.69% [E4]. Furthermore, earnings growth is actively accelerating [E65] with profits currently outpacing 1-year price growth by 38% [E55], proving that the company is starting to outperform market expectations [E55] while sitting deep in its 52-week range at just 21% of the way up [E5]. Conceded: [E14], [E26].

The most alarming weight in the evidence is the catastrophic 10-year compounded sales growth of -28% [E14], which unmasks a business of long-term structural decay despite recent top-line bounces. This severe decimation over a decade is paired with a mediocre 10-year median return on equity of just 9% [E26], proving that the company’s historical earning power is remarkably uninspiring over full economic cycles. Furthermore, the stock currently languishes near the bottom of its 52-week range, sitting a mere 21% of the way up from its low [E5], signaling persistent lack of investor confidence and downward price pressure. Conceded: the company shows robust short-term sales acceleration with a 48% trailing twelve-month growth rate [E17] and a strong recent return on equity of 24.1% [E13]. However, paying a price-to-book multiple of 3.84x on a book value of ₹ 92.1 [E2] for an entity with a deeply negative decade-long growth trajectory [E14] and a weak historical median ROE [E26] exposes investors to unjustified valuation risk.

Conceded: 10-year compounded sales growth is -28% [E14] and the 10-year median return on equity is 9% [E26], but these historical figures completely ignore the dramatic and accelerating turnaround taking place right now. Short-term sales growth has surged to 27% over 3 years [E16] and an exceptional 48% over the trailing twelve months [E17], easily outpacing the sector median sales growth of 11.8% [E73]. This powerful top-line expansion drives surging modern profitability, evidenced by a robust current return on equity of 24.1% [E13] and a 5-year median ROE of 18% [E27] that climbs to 24% over the last 3 years [E28] and last year [E29]. Finally, the bear’s worry over a 3.84x price-to-book ratio [E2] is countered by alternative data provider key-ratios showing an extremely attractive P/B of 0.66x against a sector benchmark of 1.54x [E7], complemented by a bargain P/E of 11.6x versus the sector benchmark of 20.32x [E6] and an appealing dividend yield of 3.69% [E4].

The bull’s reliance on recent growth metrics ignores the long-term structural decay evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth rate of -28% [E14] and a mediocre 10-year median ROE of 9% [E26]. While the bull highlights recent sales acceleration [E16, E17], this volatility suggests an unstable business model rather than a permanent turnaround. Conceded: the company currently shows strong ROE [E13] and recent sales growth [E17]. However, the market remains skeptical of this performance, as the stock is languishing at only 21% of its 52-week range [E5]. Furthermore, the bull’s reliance on a 0.66x P/B ratio [E7] is contradicted by the company's own filed statements, which report a significantly higher P/B of 3.84x [E2]. Relying on conflicting valuation data [E2, E7] creates an unreliable investment thesis that fails to account for the stock's proximity to its 52-week low [E5].
